confirm.text: Four forms carried an "Unsafe conditions" selection in the OWL "What did we observe?" multi-select. Per Kelby Hammer's 09/23 guidance these are reported as items needing the technician's confirmation rather than as confirmed events — technicians may be selecting "Unsafe conditions" because they regard wellhead work as inherently unsafe. One of the four is different and is called out below.
Selected "Unsafe conditions" together with "Stop work authority was discussed":

Tyrell Sanders — XTO, HAYDEN 14-23-A 2701H, 2:14 PM, job 35472. No narrative names a condition; the "Continued" text describes routine verification of zero pressure behind valves and back-pressure valves.

1099 William Jimmy Cooper — XTO, TXL 27 UNIT 3 2771JH, 1:49 PM, job 35420. The only narrative is "Team work". No condition is described.
Selected "Stop work authority was discussed" with no "Unsafe conditions" — routine pre-job item, no action needed:
1099 Gage Gonzales — XTO, BENEDUM 3D 4H, 11:03 AM, job 35393

Ralph Forbes — XTO, TXL 27 UNIT 3 2771JH, 1:49 PM, job 35419
1099 Cindy Smith — XTO, TOM GLAVINE 31-32 01HB, 9:57 AM, job 35462
"Stop work authority utilized" was not selected on any form today. Every stop-work selection reviewed was the "discussed" item, which is routine.

Not the mis-selection pattern — 1099 Gage Gonzales, XTO, SHAQ B 38-14 4202H, 9:17 AM, job 35418. This form selected "Unsafe conditions" and its narrative names an actual condition rather than leaving the selection unsupported: "WAME, Breaking containment, job steps preformed with line of fire hazard", with the Learn entry "Establish barriers in a better manner". That is a specific hazard and a specific corrective note, so it should be treated as a real observation and followed up with him on what the barrier arrangement was and whether it was corrected before work continued. Note that his partner on the same job and ticket, Nathan Contreras (35417), did not select "Unsafe conditions" and described the same work as a routine wellhead disconnect — the two accounts of one job differ and that is worth reconciling.

Repeat appearances: Nathan Contreras appeared on the stop-work confirmation list on 09/26; he does not appear on it today. Tyrell Sanders and William Jimmy Cooper are new to this list. Trailer forms of both kinds and the equipment sections of the H2S Safety Supervision Daily Inspection Form are photo-based. A defect visible only in a photograph would not surface in this review. In particular, fire extinguisher inspection and expiration dates, first aid kit dates and 4-gas calibration dates exist only inside images, not as text, so nothing in this report confirms or rules out an expired extinguisher, kit or calibration. The one exception today is Josh Blassingame's rig-up form, which records sensor calibration dates as text — both sensors calibrated 10/05/26 and due 11/05/26, in date.

A second limitation specific to this run: it executed at 11:00 PM Central on 10/06, before the calendar day closed, so the usual follow-up search over the next morning for late-arriving submissions could not be performed. Submissions for 10/06 that land overnight or tomorrow morning are not included. Any item above reported as not received should be read with that in mind, particularly the XTO Preston 9A 101H and Preston 9C 103H air jobs, which were the latest-scheduled work on the board.
